To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inositol-specific phosphoinositides (PLC) activity is increased in low and fast hepatoma cell lines, and that PLC isoforms are more expressed at the cytosolic level.

1) the phosphatidyl-inositol-specific phosphatase is present in both cytosolic and nuclear compartments in both low and fast proliferative hepatoma cell lines; 2) the phosphatase activity is increased in hepatoma cell lines with high proliferative activity; 3) PLC delta1 and PLC delta4 are over-expressed in fast proliferating hepatocytes.
the inositol specific PLCs are involved in the control of the cell cycle and in cell proliferation and possibly in the progression of neoplastic growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the expression of PLC isoforms and their activity in hepatoma cell lines with different proliferation rate.
the study of PLC isoforms in hepatoma cell lines and with their role in the regulation of cell growth.
the role of PLCs in the cell cycle and in hepatocellular carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PLC isoform expression and distribution are not only related to cell cycle progression, but they also may play a role in cell growth and differentiation.
PLC delta isoforms could represent a potential target for cancer treatment.
PLCs are involved in the control of the proliferation of hepatoma cells and that PLC delta1 and delta4 are the isoforms that are more expressed and more active in this cell type.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PLCs are expressed in the nucleus and cytoplasm and that their activity may be modulated by the cell cycle.
the PLC isoform expression in hepatoma cell lines is related to cell proliferation rate.

PLC isoforms, and in particular PLC delta, are involved in the control of the cell cycle and in cell proliferation, and that their altered expression may be a key event in the development of neoplasia.

the PLC isoform delta1 is expressed in the cytoplamic compartment, while delta4 isoform is expressed both in the cytosolic and nuclear compartment.
